title: Polaris watch — oncall pocket notes (draft)
content:
TL;DR: Leaving the shift with a degraded tail-latency regression (p95/p99) on hosted/text-generation since 03:40 UTC. Root cause suspected: new kernel-side KV eviction behavior introduced in runtime v2.1 (PR#402). Temporary mitigation in place (prefix-level cache pin + worker restart) but needs a follow-up hotfix and a controlled canary rollback plan.

What I did this shift (chronological):
- 03:42 UTC: Pager triggered - p99 tokens latency spike on hosted/text-gen. Alert: ALERT-TOK-LATENCY-001 (page).
- 03:45: Pulled latest traces (trace ids in linked_artifacts) — saw repeated model cold starts and elevated cache miss rate on kv-store.
- 03:55: Identified correlation with runtime v2.1 rollout to blue pool (tag: runtime-v2.1-canary). Noticed eviction flood on prefix keys around 03:39.
- 04:10: Applied temporary routing: route ~25% of traffic to fallback model variant (quantized-kt-v1) to reduce load.
- 04:25: Restarted 3/5 affected workers in blue pool (graceful drain + restart) — latency improved p95 -> ~400ms but p99 still high.
- 05:00: Added prefix pin: KV_PREFIX_PIN=stable_cache for production text-gen routes (via console), which reduced cache churn dramatically.
- 05:30: Created JIRA-RWI-1289 and a minimal reproducible test case. Noted PR#402 as likely culprit.

Open issues (at handoff):
- p99 still ~2–3x baseline in bursts after traffic surges (not constant).
- Root cause triage not complete: eviction algorithm change + bursty traffic interaction hypothesized.
- Need a hotfix that throttles eviction (or falls back to LRU soft limit) and a canary rollback plan.

Quick triage matrix (how to prioritize):
- Severity: High (customer-visible latency spikes).
- Impact: Hosted API (text-generation) customers; some errors observed but most traffic returns successful responses.
- Short-term priority: stabilise p99 -> below 1s within 2 hours.
- Long-term: revert or patch runtime v2.1 eviction logic and add better metrics.

Immediate mitigations (commands & steps to run):
1) Route traffic to fallback model variant (console or API):
   - Console: Routes > text-gen > Edit rule > add 25% -> quantized-kt-v1
   - API (curl): curl -X POST https://console/api/routes/text-gen/split -d '{"variant_weights": {"runtime-v2.0":0.75,"quantized-kt-v1":0.25}}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONSOLE_TOKEN"
2) Pin prefix to reduce KV eviction churn (temporary):
   - In console env var for service: KV_PREFIX_PIN=stable_cache
3) Worker restart (graceful drain):
   - ssh to node: ssh sre@worker-N
   - drain & restart: sudo systemctl stop redwood-worker; sleep 12; sudo systemctl start redwood-worker
4) Force flush and warm-up (if rolling restarts done):
   - warm script: /opt/redwood/bin/warm_kv_cache --model text-gen --prefix stable_cache --concurrency 6

Rollback & emergency steps (if mitigations fail):
- Emergency rollback of runtime to v2.0 on blue pool via deploys UI: Deploy -> Select tag runtime-v2.0 -> Rolling restart with 3m drain.
- If console deploy not responding, run: kubectl -n production set image deploy/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:runtime-v2.0 --record
- Escalation: Page oncall-SRE-lead (team: eng-sre-leads) and CC: @Marco, @Sofia.

Checks to run on handoff (please run before accepting):
- Confirm p99/p95 on hosted/text-gen (Grafana: Prod > TextGen Latency dashboard).
- Check KV cache miss rate graph (Prod > KV-store > Miss-rate).
- Verify worker restart status (kubectl get pods -n production -l role=worker).
- Ensure traffic-split is active: curl https://console/api/routes/text-gen/status -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONSOLE_TOKEN"
- Run a synthetic load test against canary: /scripts/synthetic_textgen_test.sh --concurrency 20 --duration 60s and watch p99.

Notes / TODOs / questions (for follow-up):
- TODO: Add a metric for eviction-rate in the KV exporter (prometheus label: kv_eviction_count_total) — RWI-1291.
- TODO: Add a canary metric alert that fires earlier (p95 delta > 30% over baseline).
- Question: Did we change any memtier configuration when deploying v2.1? Slack thread #runtime-deploy mentions a memcache JVM change, need to confirm.
- Possible longer-term: Introduce soft-eviction hysteresis and allow KV shard-level backpressure.

Useful links / dashboards:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/textgen-latency
- KV metrics: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/kv-store
- Deploy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/402
- Pager: https://pagerduty.com/r/redwood/alerts/ALERT-TOK-LATENCY-001

Slack channels / people to ping (order of reach):
1) #sre-oncall (general)
2) #runtime-deploy (runtime owners) -> mention @Marco Ruiz
3) @Sofia Kim (KV owner)
4) eng-sre-leads (for escalation)

Hand-off checklist (tick before leaving):
- [ ] Confirm p99 below 1s for at least 10 min under current traffic.
- [ ] Leave note in incident timeline (JIRA RWI-1289).
- [ ] Confirm fallback route is still in effect if rollback not done.
- [ ] Add any new logs/trace ids to the ticket.

Final quick notes to next oncall (voice):
- If you see p99 spike again, don't panic — routing to quantized-kt reduces load dramatically. If that doesn't help, do the worker restart (prefer smallest pool first). If restarts are giving worse behavior, roll back runtime to v2.0.
- Keep an eye on cache miss graphs; if miss-rate drops after pin, we improved things; if it rebounds, suspect another eviction vector (look for large prefix bursts).

Random scratchpad (commands I used tonight):
- kubectl -n production get pods -l role=worker -o wide
- kubectl logs -n production pod/worker-7 --since=2h | grep -i eviction | tail -n 50
- psql -h analytics-db.prod.redwood -U readonly -c "select * from incidents where id='RWI-1289'"

— Priya
(leave me a slack message if anything weird pops up; I'm out after 09:00 PT)
